title: Solo dev: an Algebra 1 RPG for students, coded with Claude Code and painted with ChatGPT. What worked, what didn't
author: brenpsnow
selftext:
I make MathBound: Algebra I, a free browser RPG where students win battles by solving real Algebra 1 problems. It's in alpha. I designed it; Claude Code wrote the code, story text and question templates; ChatGPT's image model painted the art; the music and sound effects came from AI audio tools.

Play (no sign-up): https://play.mathbound.org/alg1/?src=reddit-aigamedev

Things that were harder than expected:
- Age-appropriate art. The players are 13 to 15, and image models drift toward chibi and cute. I had to repaint the heroes older, and I check every sheet for modest clothes and poses.
- Consistency across about 48 batches of art. What helped: the prompts live in the repo, with reference images for each character and region.
- The math has to be right. Questions come from the game's own engine and are checked by automated tests, never from a model while students play.
- Taste. Claude can't see whether a painting works or hear whether a sound fits, so it puts candidates on a page and I choose.

Questions for this sub: how do you keep a character's look stable across dozens of batches? And how do you handle the "is this AI?" reaction when you post elsewhere?
